reasoning: The deepseek model successfully reviewed all 7 files and found them safe. The PKGBUILD downloads a .deb from the official cursor.com domain with pinned SHA-256 checksums, extracts it, and performs standard Electron app packaging modifications (tray injection via local Python script, AppArmor profile installation, conditional SUID for chrome-sandbox). The helper scripts (extract-asar.py, linux-tray.cjs, grok-bot.sh) are benign utilities for Electron app customization with no network exfiltration or obfuscated code. The qwen model's inconclusive verdict was due entirely to API errors (HTTP 400, LLMResponseError) on 3 files, not suspicious findings. The openrouter report is advisory-only and also suffered from tool errors. No evidence of malicious injection was found.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from tool failures, not substantive security concerns. The qwen model encountered API errors when reviewing PKGBUILD, LICENSE, and extract-asar.py, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and found them safe. The openrouter report (advisory-only) also experienced errors on grok-bot.sh and .SRCINFO. There is no actual disagreement about the safety of the code; the inconclusive verdicts are artifacts of model/API failures.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review PKGBUILD, LICENSE, and extract-asar.py due to API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError, LLMResponseError)
openrouter model failed to review grok-bot.sh (LLMResponseError) and .SRCINFO (parse error due to model output degradation into gibberish)
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, model output degradation) should not override successful reviews from other models. When one model fails to review files but another succeeds, the successful review should determine the verdict.
Implement detection for model output degradation (gibberish, incomplete responses, repeated counting loops) and automatically retry or fall back to another model.

The audit tool should distinguish between 'inconclusive due to suspicious findings' and 'inconclusive due to tool errors' and handle them differently in the final verdict calculation - tool errors should not block a safe verdict when other models have successfully reviewed the same files.
